CHronoZ | Initial monthly correlation analysis¶

tl;dr¶

The saved run analyzes 27 native monthly series and 351 unique variable pairs. Weekly and quarterly variables (9 series) are excluded. Each pair has 199-1290 shared one-month changes, above the 60-observation minimum.

  • Strongest positive transformed Pearson pair: Industrial Production / Total Capacity Utilization: r=0.9837, n=714, 1967-02 to 2026-07.
  • Most negative transformed Pearson pair: Nonfarm Payroll Employment / Unemployment Rate: r=-0.8786, n=941, 1948-02 to 2026-08.
  • Raw-level matrices are diagnostic only because long-term trends can generate spurious correlation.
  • Five changes spanning a missing calendar month were suppressed. No observations were filled or resampled.

These are contemporaneous associations, not causal or predictive findings. Full results, source fingerprints, sample sizes, and exports follow below. This summary describes the saved run; rerunning the final summary cell reports current inputs.

Context & Methods¶

This is exploratory statistical co-movement, not evidence of causality, economic transmission, a leading relationship, or predictive power. No model is trained.

Key assumptions¶

  • Inputs: data/cleaned/series_metadata.csv, the referenced cleaned CSVs, and data/audit/data_cleaning_audit.csv. Cleaning remains in dataCleansing.py.
  • Both expected and inferred frequency must be monthly. Weekly/quarterly series and frequency disagreements are reported and excluded; nothing is resampled.
  • Join on the actual observation date, with no interpolation or filling. All current monthly inputs use month-start dates; a different convention stops for review.
  • Use pairwise complete observations with at least 60 shared months per pair. Each pair can cover a different period; matrices are not restricted to a common window.
  • Percent change is 100 * (current / previous - 1) for explicitly listed positive quantities. First differences are used for rates (percentage points) and hours (hours).
  • A one-month change requires two consecutive calendar months. Missing October 2025 observations also make November 2025 changes unavailable for the affected series. Dropping NaNs does not make September and November adjacent months.
  • Rankings are descriptive: outliers, different histories, trends, multiple comparisons, and structural changes can affect them. Changes do not guarantee stationarity.

Run: use the Python kernel with requirements-notebook.txt installed, then Restart Kernel and Run All. The root is found from either the project or notebook/ directory. Only outputs/correlation/ is written; source CSVs are never changed.

Results¶

5. RAW LEVEL CORRELATION - DIAGNOSTIC ONLY¶

Many macroeconomic level series contain long-term trends. Raw-level correlation can therefore be spurious and must not be interpreted as evidence that two variables have a meaningful economic relationship. Pearson measures linear co-movement; Spearman measures rank co-movement. Both use paired available data.

Saved raw-level Pearson and Spearman matrices (diagnostic only).

9. Heatmaps¶

All panels share the same zero-centered scale from -1 to +1. Grey means undefined correlation (insufficient overlap or no variation). Category boundaries follow metadata order. Exact coefficients and sample sizes are available in CSV files.

Axes and report tables use full dataset titles. Internal series IDs remain available in the source code and the display-name mapping in provenance.json.

Raw levels expose broad shared trends. Use the change panels below for the requested exploratory comparison; high raw-level correlation alone is not economic evidence.

Pearson is sensitive to large observations. The next panel compares ranks using the same transformation and pairwise availability rules.

Takeaways¶

12. Computed summary and provenance¶

  • Monthly variables: 27; transformed: 27.
  • Raw coverage: 1913-01-01 to 2026-08-01; change coverage: 1913-02-01 to 2026-08-01.
  • Unique pairs: 351; defined Pearson: 351; defined Spearman: 351.
  • Highest positive transformed Pearson: Industrial Production / Total Capacity Utilization: r=0.9837, n=714, 1967-02 to 2026-07.
  • Most negative transformed Pearson: Nonfarm Payroll Employment / Unemployment Rate: r=-0.8786, n=941, 1948-02 to 2026-08.
  • Change overlap: 199 to 1290 observations; below 60: 0 pairs.
  • Frequency exclusions: Initial Claims, SLOOS: Banks Tightening C&I Lending Standards, SLOOS: Stronger Demand for C&I Loans, Delinquency Rate on Business Loans, Reserve Balances with Federal Reserve Banks, Federal Reserve Total Assets, Real Exports of Goods and Services, Real Imports of Goods and Services, Nonfarm Business Sector Labor Productivity.
  • Missing transformation exclusions: None.

Interpretation: these are contemporaneous, pairwise associations with different historical windows. The rankings do not establish causality, leading relationships, or predictive power. Raw-level trends and extreme observations can influence correlations; Pearson/Spearman comparisons are diagnostic. No benchmark, z-score, PCA, clustering, regime, or trained model is produced.
